principles.text: In a strong bull market most people are not bullish enough; when the chart is far more bullish than the sentiment, lean long and do not try to call the top.
After a shake-out or mistake, do not avoid the same stock or direction; it is fine to re-buy the same name at a higher price.
The strongest pullback entries stack multiple support levels at once (21 EMA, anchored VWAP, unfilled gap, 150 EMA, weekly 9 EMA); the more confluence, the more edge.
Avoid choppy stocks that ignore or whipsaw around the moving averages (lots of wicks/shakeouts); favor names that respect EMAs and follow through cleanly.
Size with the stop ~95% of the time; only on rare very-high-conviction setups (e.g. the gold/silver short) risk a larger 1-1.5%.
When you find yourself saying a stock 'should go to 1000/2000' or talking about yachts/supercars/leveraged ETFs, that is a tell you are near the end of the run.
The shift from breakouts to pullbacks is forced by a faster market; to keep a tight stop you must buy the intraday pullback before the stock rallies back to the highs.
